title: Nonlinear Operational Regime Derivation
purpose: Define the nonlinear operational regime as a derived RT classification selected when orientation-governed continuation becomes residue-conditioned, history-dependent, threshold-sensitive, feedback-coupled, or context-deforming so local composition is not preserved.

core_definition.NL: The nonlinear operational regime derived from RT_core when orientation-governed continuation is residue-conditioned, history-dependent, threshold-sensitive, feedback-coupled, or context-deforming such that local composition is not preserved.
core_definition.trace_requirement: Every NL-classified regime must constructively trace to RT_core.

derivation_rule.condition: A regime is NL-classified iff its oriented continuation fails L-classification because residue, history, admissibility, feedback, threshold, or context changes the composition rule.

governance_rules.name: Derived Nonlinear Classification
governance_rules.statement: NL is a derived regime classification, not a primitive mathematics.

governance_rules.name: Representation Downstream
governance_rules.statement: NL may support nonlinear-algebraic representation only after its RT derivation is declared.

governance_rules.name: Positive Deformation Source
governance_rules.statement: NL is not merely the negation of L; it requires a positive deformation source such as residue, history, threshold, feedback, or context.

deferred_items: Formal boundary between L and NL
effects: Registers the nonlinear regime as a governed derived classification.
Keeps nonlinear-algebraic representation downstream of RT derivation.
Preserves RT_core as the trace source for NL.

notes: Orientation classification remains the governing classifier.
Future mixed or transitional regimes attach after this nonlinear regime derivation.
The nonlinear regime is derived from RT_core through orientation-governed classification.
Nonlinear-algebraic representation is permitted only after RT derivation is declared.
This patch is governance and architecture only.
